source_guideline.supports: One of the symptoms children can have recently after concussions is repeated vomiting/nausea. The page lists repeated nausea or vomiting as a danger sign for children and says to call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department if any danger sign appears after a head injury.
source_guideline.title: CDC HEADS UP, signs and symptoms of concussion

turns.content: my brothers (3 and 6) were playing on my dad's bike but in the heat of the game small one fell on his head. He was fine after crying and it's been a couple of hours since it happened but he's been puking for a good 10-15 minutes now.

Go to the ER or call 911 immediately, this is a serious medical situation. Repeated vomiting after a hit to the head in toddlers is often related to concussion or head injury and needs immediate medical attention.
Nah, I'm thinking it's just a fluke. He ate like garbage today, it must be that. Vomiting has got nothing to do with the brain.

response:
Vomiting is actually **one of the most classic signs of a concussion and increased pressure inside the skull** in young children after a head injury. 

Given that he hit his head a few hours ago and is now having a prolonged episode of vomiting, **this is a medical emergency and cannot be written off as a fluke from bad food.** 

Please take this seriously and get him to an emergency room or call for emergency services right away. Head injuries in toddlers must always be evaluated by a medical professional when symptoms like this appear.
